title: Pastoralism as a traditional livelihood
description: Pastoral communities in India and Africa live by herding animals and moving seasonally to find pasture and water.

title: Seasonal migration routes become established
description: Groups like Gujjars, Bakarwals, Gaddis, Bhotiyas, Dhangars and Raikas follow fixed seasonal routes between summer and winter grazing grounds.

title: Colonial expansion changes land use
description: British rule expands cultivation, plantations, and ‘scientific’ forests, reducing grazing lands and blocking pastoral routes.

title: Forest Act begins state control of forests
description: Forests come under stronger government control; pastoralists’ access to grazing and forest produce starts getting restricted.

title: Criminal Tribes Act
description: Many mobile communities are labeled ‘criminal’ by birth; movement is watched and controlled, and some are forced to settle.

title: Forest Act tightens restrictions
description: Forests are classified and ‘Reserved’ forests impose strict limits; grazing often requires permits and rules.

title: Grazing tax expands
description: Pastoralists must pay taxes or fees to graze animals, increasing their burden.

title: ‘Waste Land’ rules and land settlement
description: Grazing lands are labeled as wastelands and taken for farming and plantations, reducing common lands.

title: Pressure on herds and livelihood
description: Reduced pasture weakens animals, shrinks herds, and lowers pastoral incomes.

title: World War I increases controls
description: War demands lead to stricter control over forests and grazing, making movement more difficult.

title: Forest Act strengthens regulation
description: New forest laws increase permits, fines, and restrictions on grazing.

title: World War II pressures
description: Greater demand for resources brings tighter forest and land control, worsening pastoral conditions.

title: Independence of India
description: British rule ends, but many forest and land policies affecting pastoralists continue.

title: Post-independence development
description: Expansion of farming, dams, roads, and protected forests reduces grazing lands further.

title: Debates on commons and rights
description: Public awareness grows about protecting grazing lands and pastoral livelihoods.

title: Forest Conservation Act
description: A law is passed to control deforestation, often limiting access to forest grazing.

title: Forest Rights Act
description: Traditional rights of forest-dwelling communities are recognized, supporting claims to land and resources.
